doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Five drum sets in the house and his mother at the piano
summary: His mother accepted the drumming, once playing piano with the brothers on Willow Weep for Me and asking about brushes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So how did your mother feel about having five drum sets in the house?

She was accepting. You know? But one of my favorite moments was when we had five sets going, me and Tony and Eric and Nicholas and my dad, all playing — or actually my dad wasn’t there, he was off in his studio I think, but the four sets of drums were going and my mother was playing piano and we were playing “Willow Weep for Me.” She was pretty good. And something else she would play, “When Sunny Gets Blue” but the four guys, I think I might have been 15 and then the ages range on down. And everybody was into Led Zeppelin and John Mayall and the Heartbreakers and the Beatles and the Stones and stuff and we’re banging away on “Willow Weep for Me” and my mother turns around from the piano and said, “What about brushes?” So she was very understanding and there were rare — a rare instance where she would say na, could you hold off a minute. You know I would get home from school and say, “Mom can I drum?” And, “Okay, all right, ‘till dinnertime anyway.” Only rarely would she say, “Can you hold off until four o’clock? Can you wait until five o’clock?” But she was always encouraging © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

whoever it was. And usually the sets were scattered. Everybody had their set in their room but if there was a rehearsal or a jam session or something like that we’d bring down all the sets so there would be five sets set up and an acoustic piano.
